1) the GPCR-pathways is robust to the localization of the G-protein; 2) above a certain threshold of the G-proteins concentration, localization of the G-alpha protein hampers its translocation to the cell membrane; 3) this effect is due to physical occupation constraints of G-alpha molecules, which prevent the translocation of G-alpha molecules from the cytosol to the cell membrane.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the localization mechanism is a double-edged sword: while it increases robustness, it may also hinder the translocation process.
localization of the signal-coupling protein Gβγ in a subcellular compartment is not a necessary condition to obtain a robust signal transduction mechanism, but it is an efficient one.

the localization of the signal-carring molecule is not a good strategy to increase the signal efficiency, as it is often assumed, but it is rather a way to avoid the obstruction of the signal transduction mechanism by the mere occupation of the space by the signal-carryng molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
localization is a double-edged sword, and that the efficiency of the signal-carying process is a function of the density and of the localization degree.
, in a crowded environment, the signal transduction efficiency is not only dependent on the number of molecules, but also on the way they are distributed within the cell.
the signal-carryng efficiency of a molecular species is enhanced by localization, but only above a threshold concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the signal-carryng efficiency is enhanced when a molecular species is localized in a region of the cytoplasm, but this effect is limited by a threshold concentration.
the localization of molecules in the cytoplasm is not a mere physical constraint but rather a functional mechanism that may be exploited to regulate the efficiency of a given pathway.
the spatial organization of the cytosolic environment is crucial for the efficiency of signal transduction.
